messages:
Maya (Director SRE): thanks everyone — quick follow-up from the all-hands: can we clarify the release cadence & oncall expectations? specifically: weekly vs biweekly releases, who owns handoffs, what exactly is our quality bar before pushing to prod?
Diego (VP Eng): good call. short answer: aim for weekly small releases for service-level changes; biweekly for coordinated, infra-wide rollouts. exceptions for security/urgent fixes.
Maya (Director SRE): when you say weekly, do you mean a single org-wide window or per-team schedules?
Diego (VP Eng): per-team windows, with a default team release slot on Thursdays 10–12PT. if you need a different slot, coordinate with release eng. cross-team releases coordinate via the release calendar.
Leo (Eng Manager): adding — please try to keep changes small (<= 2 services) for weekly windows. Big refactors should go into the biweekly planning lane. small changes reduce blast radius and make rollbacks simpler.
Riley (Release Eng): ops note: our canary policy is 5% for 30m, then 25% for 30m, then 100% if healthy. automatic rollback on error budget breach or >1% error rate. we can tweak per-service in the release config. example deploy command: `./release.sh deploy --service=model-serving --canary 5%`
Sam (Product): curious about quality bar — what automated checks are mandatory vs. recommended?
Diego (VP Eng): mandatory: unit tests, integration tests for changed paths, infra smoke, canary, and perf regression gate on the critical path. recommended: load tests and customer-facing QA for big UX changes.
Maya (Director SRE): and SLAs — are teams expected to hit the same targets across product tiers?
Ava (CEO): public hosted customers have SLA tiers. baseline internal SLOs: 99.9% availability for critical endpoints; P99 latency targets depend on the API (embeddings vs generation) — your team PM will have the specific numbers. if you see sustained regressions, escalate to SRE and your PM.
Leo (Eng Manager): who pages on a Sev2 incident during releases?
Riley (Release Eng): on-call owner for the service gets first page. release engineer watches the rollout and will assist. if the oncall is overloaded, the release owner (PR author) gets notified. our policy: page for Sev2/Sev1; Sev3 can be slack-first unless it impacts customers.
Maya (Director SRE): handoffs — do we have a standard post-release checklist and who signs off?
Riley (Release Eng): yes — post-release checklist lives in `docs/release_playbook.md`. sign-off: release engineer + oncall + author for the change. checklist items: canary metrics green, logs smoke, latency within threshold, and no new customer errors.
Sam (Product): can we add a quick rollback play in the playbook for feature flags? some teams rely on flags rather than full rollbacks.
Diego (VP Eng): agreed — add a feature-flag rollback template. action: @Riley please add to playbook and share a PR by EOW.
Riley (Release Eng): on it. I'll file the PR and ping this thread.
ops-bot: scheduled canary run for `model-serving` started at 1764800200 — 5% for 30m.
Maya (Director SRE): thanks. last ask — can we get a single-page doc summarizing: weekly slot, canary policy, who to page, and minimal preflight checklist? something to share with new hires.
Diego (VP Eng): yes — I'll put together a one-pager and post it in #devex. ETA next Tue.
Ava (CEO): appreciate the follow-up. short doc will help teams ship safer and faster. :thumbsup:
Maya (Director SRE): perfect. if anyone has edge cases (air-gapped, private deploys) DM me and Riley. otherwise thanks all — closing this thread after Riley's PR.
